citation.title: A roentgenographic cephalometric study of 144 Chinese with normal occlusion
citation.journal: Chung-Hua Kou Chiang Ko Tsa Chih (Chinese Journal of Stomatology)

secondHand.via: Moate & Darendeliler 2002, Tables I, II, III and IV

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08: norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 87 differences (logs/task9a2-compare-<id>.log). Every mean and SD of both extractors re-read from the page images (PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24), and the settled file checked by script against a third, independent reading of the pages (the table in sets.test.ts). Decisions: (0) Source text normalised to one pattern giving table, page, row and column with sex and age (a and b worded it differently; prose only). Adult rows: a gave [18, 40], b no band -> [18, 40] with the P18 note (merge notes). b's UFH:LFH% rows (#29) not entered: the merge notes rule the printed UFH:LFH ratio is not a catalogue measurement (do not compute ratios). (1) b only, each confirmed on Table II p. 21 and kept: facial axis males 11 y 83 ± 1 (Fu male column); Y axis 66 ± 3 males and females 11 y (Fu columns); gonial angle females 11 y 124 ± 9 (right-aligned under 'Female Fu'; a missed all four). (2) Y axis and facial axis a same / b close -> close: the compilation defines neither (see each definitionNote). Fix round 1 (8 Oct): facial axis rows -> different, not used (owner FAX-1); each 11-year row carries the 'may not be a separate group' note. (3) Selection a class-I / b class-I-balanced -> class-I-balanced: Class I occlusion with a good-looking profile (text p. 21). Page images: PDF pp. 2-6 = journal pp. 20-24 (Tables I-VI), rendered at 2000 px.

caveats: Quoted second-hand from Moate & Darendeliler 2002 (Aust Orthod J 18:19-26, a compilation of published Chinese cephalometric norms), Tables I, II, III and IV; the original paper was not read. The compilation rounds every mean and SD to whole numbers (Lew's soft tissue to 0.5) and gives no landmark, plane or method definitions.
The compilation states no film scale or magnification for any study; assumed true size (owner ruling M-2).

144 Chinese students in Beijing selected for Class I occlusion and a pleasing profile, in three average-age groups: 9, 13.9 and 18.6 years (text p. 21). The sex split and group sizes are not given. Table III's 13-year column is read as the 13.9-year group and Table IV's '18 Years +' as the 18.6-year group (18-40 by convention).

Table II prints Fu 11-year columns (males and females), but the text names only the 9, 13.9 and 18.6-year groups, and most 11-year values repeat the 13-year ones (SNA 83, SNB 79, ANB 4, ANS-Me 67 and 62): the 11-year group may not be a real group. Kept as tabled (merge notes).
Fu's 11-year facial axis SD is printed ± 1 (Table II, p. 21), much narrower than every other facial-axis SD in the compilation (3-6); kept as printed.
Not entered (not catalogue measurements; no ratio computed): N-ANS and UFH:LFH% (every group).
Table V (p. 24) averages several studies; it is not entered for this study (merge notes).
